title: Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · sec1-p3】The discovery of gas signaling molecules has provided a novel approach for treating ED. Gas signaling molecules are a class of endogenous gas mediators, including NO, carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), etc. These molecules play important physiological regulatory roles in the body and share the following common characteristics: small molecular weight, free penetration through biological membranes, short half-life, synthesis by specific enzymes, and concentration-dependent biological effects.4,5,6 In the male reproductive system, gas signaling molecules play a crucial role in the physiological process of penile erection by regulating vascular smooth muscle tone, endothelial function, and neural signal transmission.4,5,6 Therefore, in-depth exploration of the functions of the gas signaling molecule network in the pathophysiological mechanism of ED and the development of novel therapeutic strategies based on these molecules, such as regulating their synthesis, release, delivery or signaling pathways, have become a promising direction in the current ED research field, which is expected to provide innovative solutions to overcome the limitations of existing PDE5i treatments. The primary research purpose of this review is to systematically evaluate and synthesize the roles of gas signaling molecules, specifically NO, CO, and H2S, within the physiological and pathological frameworks of ED.

【Introduction · sec1-p1】Erectile dysfunction (ED) is one of the most common male diseases. Due to the inability to achieve or maintain a penile erection of sufficient strength, it has a significant negative impact on the quality of life of patients. Epidemiological data show that about 50% of men over 40 years old have ED to varying degrees, and its prevalence increases with age.1

【Introduction · sec1-p2】The treatment options for ED include psychological interventions, lifestyle modifications, oral medications, intracavernous drug injections, vacuum erection devices, shockwave therapy, and penile prosthesis implantation, among others. Currently, phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitors (PDE5i), such as Sildenafil, Udinafil, and Tadalafil, are considered the first-line oral treatments for ED.2 The mechanism of action of PDE5i drugs is to enhance penile erectile hardness by increasing the level of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP). Due to the dependence of this class of drugs on the nitric oxide (NO) signaling pathway, the response rate to treatment in patients with chronic neurogenic ED is relatively low, and the clinical efficacy is still not satisfactory.3

sections.text:
《Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · sec30-p13】Can we find biomarkers to identify ED subtypes best suited for gas-based vs. traditional therapy?

【Conclusion · sec30-p1】Although gas signaling molecules show great potential in the treatment of ED, their clinical translation is still limited by delivery bottlenecks caused by short molecular half-life and high diffusivity, as well as the strict requirements for dose-effect control and the heterogeneity of ED pathology. Current experimental designs also have limitations, mainly manifesting as an overreliance on animal models while neglecting interspecies anatomical differences, and a lack of long-term in vivo safety evaluation and real-time monitoring of local concentrations. Therefore, it is urgent to achieve precise targeting and “on-demand release” through multidisciplinary approaches using responsive nanocarriers (such as nanoparticles and hydrogels), and to develop novel stable gas donors. Combining omics technologies to carry out personalized precision medicine will facilitate the transition of this therapy from basic research to clinical application, offering new treatment hope for patients with refractory ED.

sections.title: 图表阅读

《Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1 · mgr.MEDGASRES-D-25-00333-F1】Figure 1 Neural regulatory network of penile erection.The central system (limbic system, hypothalamus, and brainstem) is responsible for integrating multisource sensory signals and transmitting them via descending pathways to the spinal erection centers (T11–L2 and S2–S4), with the sacral parasympathetic nuclei initiating erection through the pelvic nerves. In peripheral regulation, parasympathetic nerves release ACh to activate M3 receptors and promote NO synthesis for smooth muscle relaxation, while sympathetic nerves maintain detumescence through NE and α1 receptors, and somatic nerves are responsible for sensory input and muscle contraction. Additionally, the NANC system enhances erectile function via VIP, CGRP, and purine substances, working synergistically with NO through the cAMP pathway and potassium channels. Created with BioRender.com. Ach: Acetylcholine; ATP: adenosine triphosphate; cAMP: cyclic adenosine monophosphate; CGRP: calcitonin gene-related peptide; NANC: non-adrenergic, non-cholinergic; NE: norepinephrine; NO: nitric oxide; VIP: vasoactive intestinal peptide.

【Figure 2 · mgr.MEDGASRES-D-25-00333-F2】Figure 2 The sexual stimulation triggered NO-sGC-cGMP pathway and its downstream regulatory processes.In parasympathetic nerve terminals and vascular endothelial cells, nNOS and eNOS convert L-arginine into NO. NO diffuses into smooth muscle cells and activates sGC, which catalyzes the conversion of GTP to cGMP. Subsequently, cGMP activates PKG, which lowers intracellular Ca2+ concentration through the following three mechanisms: (1) inhibiting VGCC to reduce calcium influx; (2) enhancing SERCA activity to promote calcium reuptake; and (3) inhibiting MLCK activity. These pathways ultimately lead to smooth muscle relaxation and penile erection. In addition, PDE5 is responsible for degrading cGMP into 5′-GMP, and PDE5i maintain high cGMP levels by blocking this degradation process, thereby improving erectile function. Created with BioRender.com. 5′-GMP: Guanosine 5′-monophosphate; cGMP: cyclic guanosine monophosphate; eNOS: endothelial nitric oxide synthase; GTP: guanosine triphosphate; MLCK: myosin light-chain kinase; nNOS: neuronal nitric oxide synthase; NO: nitric oxide; PDE5: phosphodiesterase type 5; PDE5i: phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors; SERCA: sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase; sGC: soluble guanylyl cyclase; VGCC: voltage-gated calcium channel.

【Figure 3 · mgr.MEDGASRES-D-25-00333-F3】Figure 3 The molecular mechanisms on endocrine and metabolic factors regulate erectile function.Androgens play a key positive role by enhancing nNOS/eNOS expression, maintaining smooth muscle phenotype stability, and regulating central neural circuits; estrogens exhibit concentration-dependent bidirectional regulatory characteristics, with low concentrations promoting erection synergistically through ERα, while high concentrations may exert inhibitory effects via ERβ, highlighting the importance of hormonal balance; metabolic factors reduce NO bioavailability by inducing oxidative stress, accumulating AGEs, and damaging the endothelial barrier, elucidating the molecular mechanisms by which diabetes and atherosclerosis lead to ED. Created with BioRender.com. AGE: Advanced glycation end-products; CONC: concentration; ED: erectile dysfunction; eNOS: endothelial nitric oxide synthase; ER: estrogen receptor; nNOS: neuronal nitric oxide synthase.
